card.name: Dabke
card.tagline: Levantine stomping line dance led by a handkerchief-waving lawweeh
card.profile: Dabke is the Levantine folk line dance performed at weddings and celebrations across Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Palestine and Iraq (Wikipedia). Dancers link hands in a line or semicircle and stamp and jump in synchronised six-beat patterns; the line is led by a lawweeh (raas) who waves a handkerchief or string of beads (masbaha), improvising leaps and breaks (Wikipedia; iHeritage). The name derives from Levantine Arabic dabaka, 'stamping of the feet'; folklore links its stomping origin to communally tamping mud rooftops (Bayt Al Fann).
card.insight: Though a powerful emblem of Lebanese identity, dabke is shared across the whole Levant and is not uniquely Lebanese. After the launch of the Baalbek International Festival in 1956, Soviet dance expert Igor Moiseyev was invited to assess Lebanese folk traditions and proposed a standardized choreography (The Beiruter; iHeritage).
